principle.name: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
principle.description: A class should have only one reason to change. When analyzing a class, list all the reasons it could change. Each reason represents a separate responsibility.

example.scenario: A service class that does data access, algorithm execution, and orchestration
example.good: Split into: - Repository (data access) - Strategy (algorithm) - Service (orchestration)
example.bad: Keeping all three responsibilities in one class with private methods. This makes testing and maintenance harder.

principle.name: Dependency Injection (DI)
principle.description: Dependencies should be injected via constructor, not hard-coded or created inside the class. This makes testing easier and allows swapping implementations.

example.scenario: A class that needs a database repository

principle.name: Keep existing behavior intact
principle.description: Refactoring should not change observable behavior. Always run tests and verify that the code works the same way after changes.

convention.rule: Use Protocol classes for dependency interfaces
convention.example: class RepositoryProtocol(Protocol): def get_entries(self, id: str) -> List[Dict]: ...

convention.rule: One file per class (except closely related small classes)
